SÃDERTÃLJE, Sweden , Oct. 28, 2026 /PRNewswire/ --
Resilient performance with continued growth in services
Sales revenue increased by 5 percent to SEK 49.1 billion (46.9)
Adjusted return on sales was 12.3 percent (11.1)
Deliveries increased by 3 percent to 22,086 vehicles, whereof Battery Electric Vehicles (BEV) amounted to 247 units (159)
Order intake decreased by 2 percent to 20,098 vehicles, whereof Battery Electric Vehicles (BEV) amounted to 511 units (133)
Scania delivered a resilient performance in the third quarter, with improved profitability compared with the same period last year.
Sales revenue increased compared with the third quarter last year. Profitability improved, supported by higher truck deliveries, a favourable product mix, continued growth in the services business and favourable currency effects.
Overall truck order intake remained at a stable level although regional market trends varied. Activity strengthened in parts of Asia and Africa, while orders declined in Europe and Latin America. Battery-electric truck orders increased compared with the same period last year, although overall adoption lags behind where it should be.
Scania continued to invest in future competitiveness through new products, digital services and industrial capabilities, while maintaining a strong focus on efficiency and cost discipline across the business.
"Scania delivered a resilient performance in the third quarter, with improved profitability and continued growth in our service business. Our strong customer offering and focus on efficiency supported our performance as demand varied across markets," says Christian Levin, President and CEO of Scania and TRATON GROUP.
Read Scania's Q3 2026 Performance Summary and the full CEO comment here: www.scania.com/performance-summary
Scania's full financial performance can be found in the segment reporting of TRATON Group's interim statement.
